brief: Raymond James's weekly earnings tracker reports 84% of S&P 500 firms have beaten 3Q26 EPS estimates, above the 10-year average of 77%, putting the index on track for a third consecutive quarter of EPS growth above 25%. Aggregate figures show 31.3% year-over-year EPS growth, an 83.9% beat rate, and 14.1% sales growth, led by Energy (156.2% EPS growth, 100% beat rate) and Information Technology (67.8% EPS growth, 94.5% beat rate). This week's calendar is dominated by NVIDIA, reporting Tuesday, which the note frames as the latest read on AI infrastructure demand; Walmart and Target report later in the week and are flagged as the gauge of household purchasing behavior and discretionary-demand resilience heading into year end. A transcript-spotlight section adds three management comments with no independent analysis attached: KKR says it deployed $20bn in Q3 ($98bn trailing twelve months, up 15%) against a record $146bn of dry powder; Constellation Energy says the market overreacted to midterm-election fears that Democrats would block data-center construction; Applied Materials expects 2027 to be another record year as AI drives multi-year semiconductor demand.
